graphEvents.label: A bare document read counts as a start
Claude alone owns the host-expansion start shape

label: A start row counts as started without any write: startState accepts a document read, a reported COMMAND start or a host expansion and never consults a write boundary.

The two start functions disagree about a bare document read: startedCommand requires a write boundary before a read counts, so one transcript can be a start under the start rate and not under the decline count.

The start vocabulary is runtime-asymmetric: hostExpanded recognises Claude Code expansion tag, which records a start the model never chose, and Claude is the only one of six runtimes that can produce it.
Nothing prints which shape produced a start: byPolicy carries counts and commandStartRuns lists row, run and command without the shape, so the mix cannot be recovered from the summary.

The fix is a measurement field not a product change: recording the start shape per scored row and printing its distribution per runtime would make the five runtimes 15-row start counts comparable without touching any command, vector, brief byte or floor input.
